stem:
Neil simplifies $\dfrac{7^{8}}{7^{3}}$ for counting-number exponents with the same nonzero base.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $\dfrac{7^{8}}{3^{3}}=7^{8-3}$, as if different bases still allowed subtracting exponents.
$\dfrac{7^{3}}{7^{8}}=7^{3-8}$ is covered by the same stated rule for $a>b$ counting exponents with no further condition.
$\dfrac{7^{8}}{7^{3}}=7^{8-3}=7^{5}$, because the bases are the same and nonzero.
The value is $7$, because $7$ is the printed base shown most clearly.

teacher.key_rationale: Same nonzero base and $a>b$ give $7^{8-3}=7^{5}$. Different bases omit the same-base condition. Extending the $a>b$ rule to $3<8$ without further work is a scope error. Picking the printed base captures a surface feature.
